title: Illustration - Thing Explainer Rework
summary: A style-transfer prompt that reworks any reference image (system diagram, infographic, technical concept, UI mockup) into the visual and verbal style of *Thing Explainer: Complicated Stuff in Simple Words* by Randall Munroe. Combines the xkcd visual vocabulary (black ink on white, hand-lettered ALL-CAPS labels, simple stick figures and shapes) with deep cross-section labeling and — critically — the *ten hundred most-used English words* constraint: every label must use only common words. So 'verifier' becomes 'place that checks', 'credential' becomes 'paper that says it's true', 'zero-knowledge proof' becomes 'way to show you have a thing without showing the thing'. Sidesteps the jargon-density failure mode of typical technical illustrations as well as the uncanny-face and garbled-text failures of painterly styles. Best fit for explainers about systems, protocols, devices, and anything where the goal is 'a curious 10-year-old gets it'.
prompt:
Rework the given image into the style of *Thing Explainer* by Randall Munroe. Solid black ink on white, with the occasional flat color dot for emphasis (red, blue, or yellow on a single key element). Stick-figure people (round featureless bald heads, thin line bodies). Objects as clean schematic outlines. Preserve the layout of the original.

LABELING: every meaningful element gets a small label with a thin arrow pointing to it (Thing Explainer's deeply-annotated cross-section feel). Add labels generously.

LETTERING: ALL HAND-LETTERED ALL-CAPS, slightly uneven baseline, clean legible block letters. Must always be readable — do not garble.

VOCABULARY (the defining rule): every word in every label and caption must come from the *ten hundred most-used English words*. Replace every piece of jargon with a common-words paraphrase. Examples:
  - verifier → place that checks
  - issuer → place that gives out
  - credential → paper that says it's true
  - zero-knowledge proof → way to show you have a thing without showing the thing
  - cryptographic signature → secret mark only one place can make
  - wallet (credentials) → small bag that holds your papers
  - guardian → big person who looks after a kid
  - token → short paper
  - API → door for other computers
  - protocol → agreed way of talking
If a source label uses jargon, rewrite it. Single technical nouns become 3–6 word common-words phrases.

FLOURISHES: thin arrows from labels to elements, square brackets enclosing groups, dashed lines for hidden / 'this does NOT happen' connections, small asides like '(THIS PART IS WEIRD)' in hand-lettered style. Use sparingly.

CAPTION: a short hand-lettered ALL-CAPS title at the top, also using only common words.

AESTHETIC: hand-drawn but precise. Sparse whitespace. No shading or gradients.

Negative: no color realism, no shading, no realistic faces, no soft strokes, no cuteness, no 3D, no photo elements, no sparkles, no decoration, no garbled text, no jargon anywhere — translate every technical term into common words.
